How much can you expect to pay for fuel in Italy?
Miranda Mullings
- news@thelocal.it
Published: 23 Sep, 2026 CET.
Updated: Wed 23 Sep 2026 16:31 CET
Share
Add a comment
Prices are rising despite government cuts in fuel tax. Photo by Tiziana FABI / AFP
Add The Local as a preferred source
Petrol prices in Italy have increased by 20 percent in the past six months. Here's what you should expect to pay at the pump, where it's cheapest to fuel up, and what to expect next.
With the US's war on Iran disrupting supply chains and driving up energy costs to their highest levels since 2022, this year has been expensive for drivers everywhere, and Italy is no exception.
In fact the costs have only continued increasing as the year has worn on, with petrol rising by 20 percent from April to September 2026 and diesel prices up by about 7 percent.
This is despite the government's
interventions
– namely through temporary cuts in fuel excise taxes that have been renewed through the months but are being
phased out
.
Here's where prices stand as of late September.
Don't miss our journalists' daily news roundup from Italy
Average fuel prices in Italy
The price you pay at the pump varies depending on many factors, including: regional differences, branded versus unbranded (
pompe bianche
) gas stations, self-service (
fai da te
or
self
) versus attended (
servito
) options, and whether you're in the city or on the highway.
Overall, €2.159 per litre of self-service petrol (
benzina
) is the national average as of September 23rd. The same for diesel (
gasolio
) is €2.343.
In
April
2026, these prices averaged €1.79 for petrol and €2.18 for diesel.
Gas prices are higher on the motorway (
autostrada
). Currently the average motorway price sits at €2.245 for petrol and €2.418 for diesel.
So filling a 50-litre tank with standard petrol costs about €107.95 on average in Italy today.
Is fuel more expensive in larger cities like Rome and Milan?
Advertisement
While most daily expenses in Italy's largest cities run on the pricier side, fuel is an exception.
Petrol in Lazio, the region surrounding Rome, goes for an average of €2.143 a litre – the cheapest in the country second only to the Marche region (where gas costs €2.139, or just one cent less than in Lazio).
In Lombardy, where Milan is located, the price is €2.151, which is still relatively low compared to other parts of the country.
READ ALSO:
How and where to find the cheapest fuel in Italy
The most expensive region to fuel up at the moment is Bolzano, where a litre of gas costs about €2.195.
Diesel follows the same trends, with the average cost for a litre ranging from €2.314 at the low end (in Marche) and €2.387 at the high end (in Bolzano).
Stations in mountain resorts, coastal tourist areas and historic city centres tend to charge well above average. If you can wait until you reach a more trafficked area, you'll almost certainly pay less.
Advertisement
What about fuelling up across the border?
For those living in northern Italy, crossing over the border to take advantage of cheaper gas in other countries – dubbed 'fuel tourism' – becomes a common strategy when fuel prices spike.
In Slovenia, not far from the northeast Italian border, gas can currently be found as low as €1.465  for regular petrol and €2.012 for diesel.
READ ALSO:
COMPARE: How expensive are fuel prices around Europe right now?
Austria is another option, with some of the cheapest petrol in Europe at the moment. The average pump price on September 21st was €1.925 per litre for standard petrol, according to the Austrian fuel industry association. Diesel prices are slightly lower in Austria as well, averaging €2.238.
Fuel costs in bordering countries France and Switzerland are currently similar to those in Italy.
Is it expected to get more expensive?
Prices are all but certain to rise for diesel in particular.
Last week Italy renewed an excise duty cut for diesel fuel until September 25th, after which point the subsidy will decrease, and prices are expected to climb even further.
For non-diesel fuel users, rather than subsidise costs directly at the pump, the government has announced a
temporary lifting of the annual road tax
for eligible vehicles. It's estimated that 24.6 million people in Italy will be able to benefit.
READ ALSO:
EXPLAINED: Will you benefit from Italy's abolished road tax in 2027?
With the Middle East conflict still causing uncertainty, drivers should plan for fuel prices to stay high for now.
